title: Screws
prompt: A labelled principle teaching adaptation of pages 62 and 63 uses a single-start screw held in axial bearings and a mating nut on a guided non-rotating load carriage. Turn rotates the screw and advances the nut by one pitch per revolution. Reverse backs the carriage away. Compare pitch first unloads the rig and exchanges complete compatible screw-and-nut pairs, then compares travel per turn and ideal axial force at the same applied torque. See-through shows thread engagement, guides, bearings and the physical load. A wrapped-inclined-plane drawing and force/travel arrows are overlays. Identify the carriage and interchangeable pairs as teaching fixtures. Do not morph an engaged thread or count overlays as parts.
blurb: A screw principle teaching rig compares travel and ideal force at equal torque using complete interchangeable screw and nut pairs.

physicalFixtures: load platform and fixed unloading rests
teachingControls: complete compatible pair exchange after returning the physical load to its rests
limitations: Ideal force neglects friction; actual force is lower.
Exchange is an operator teaching reset, not automatic hardware.
1988 edition remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition-union claim.
